title: Burst scheduling & reservation policy - UX roughs
content:
Purpose:
This note captures early UX wireframe ideas and backlog candidate items for a burst scheduling + reservation policy editor inside the Dedicated Capacity console. Goal is a concise, engineering-friendly page that lets platform and infra teams: define burst budgets, configure soft vs hard burst behavior, preview cost/latency impact, and create reservations that interact predictably with autoscaling policies and fallback models.

Background/context:
- We already have a pool list and basic reservation flow (see existing notes). This doc focuses on the policy surface that decides how a pool can temporarily borrow extra capacity (burst) and how reservations and autoscale rules interact.
- Primary user: infra/platform engineers and SREs managing Dedicated GPU pools for customers. Secondary user: internal solutions engineers running demos.
- Constraints: must be understandable for non-inference experts, map cleanly to server-side config (policy DSL), and surface clear safety checks (preemption, cost cap).

Personas / scenarios:
1) Platform engineer (Emma) wants to allow short-term bursts for spike traffic while preserving baseline tenants. She needs: burst window, max extra GPUs, preemption weight, and cost cap.
2) Solutions engineer (Ben) needs to reserve GPUs for customer demo slots and allow those reservations to opt-in to bursts if available.
3) SRE (Riley) wants incident-mode behavior: when an outage in a primary region occurs, burst budgets can be auto-expanded for failover lanes.

High-level UX goals:
- Single-page policy editor per pool + a global policy template gallery
- Quick preview of "what happens if" (cost estimate, latency delta, affected reservations)
- Clear explicit choices: soft-burst (best-effort) vs hard-burst (preempt current best-effort workloads)
- Tight integration with reservation flow: link from reservation modal to policy toggles
- Safety defaults and validation (daily cost cap, max concurrently burstable GPUs)

Wireframe concepts (panels):
A. Pool Policy Dashboard (list -> expanded rows)
- Left column: pool list (name, baseline GPUs, utilization %, current burst usage)
- Right column: selected pool detail (policy summary card + actions)
- Small inline sparkline per-pool showing 24h burst consumption

B. Policy Summary Card (compact)
- Policy name (editable), mode badge (default / custom / inherited), toggle active/off
- Primary knobs: max_burst_gpus (slider), burst_window_minutes (dropdown), cost_cap_daily (currency input)
- Inline quick action: "Apply template" -> opens small gallery

C. Detailed Policy Editor (modal or panel)
Sections:
  - Basic: name, description, inherit-from (global template)
  - Capacity: baseline_gpus (readonly), max_burst_gpus, burst_priority (0-100), preemption_allowed (checkbox)
  - Windowing: burst_window (5, 15, 30, 60 min), refill_rate (tokens/min)
  - Cost guardrails: max_daily_spend, notify_on_spend_thresholds (25/50/75%)
  - Incident behavior: incident_mode_override (dropdown: no-change / expand-by-% / set-to-value)
  - Reservation interactions: allow_reservation_burst (none / soft-only / preemptible)
  - Preview panel: estimated cost delta per hour/day, estimated latency improvement for 95th pct requests (rough model)

D. Reservation Flow integration
- In reservation modal, small row: "Allow burst?" toggle with explanatory tooltip and link to "Edit pool policy"
- If reservations opt into burst, show badge on reservation list: "burst-opt-in"

E. Autoscale + Burst interplay visualization
- Timeline chart with baseline capacity, autoscale curve, and burst budget overlay. Hover to see which policy applied at any time.

F. Incident Mode quick card (top-right)
- Global "Incident Mode" toggle (SREs only) that temporarily widens burst caps for targeted pools for N hours. Must require two-step confirmation. Shows audit log entry.

UX micro-copy examples:
- Soft burst tooltip: "Best-effort extra GPUs — allocated if idle capacity exists; may be revoked if higher-priority requests need baseline capacity."
- Hard burst tooltip: "Allocates extra GPUs by preempting best-effort workloads. Use sparingly; preempted jobs will be terminated or checkpointed if enabled."
- Cost preview note: "Estimates based on current pricing, recent burst consumption; actual may vary."

Backlog candidate tickets (priority rough):
1) INF-7421: Policy editor UI + DSL mapping (MVP) - high priority
   - Acceptance: create / edit / delete policy, persisted to backend config, applied to pool
2) INF-7422: Reservation modal - add "Allow burst" integration and badge - med
   - Acceptance: badge visible, reservation-level opt-in stored, enforcement in runtime stubbed
3) INF-7424: Cost estimate microservice / preview integration - med-high
   - Acceptance: preview shows hourly/day delta for sample workloads
4) INF-7427: Incident Mode workflow + audit log - high (SRE requirement)
5) INF-7430: Autoscale timeline visualization - low-med

Open questions / risks:
- Runtime mapping: do we support fractional GPU credit accounts or only integer GPUs? Affects refill token UX. (Action: sync with runtime team).
- Pricing model variance across regions — how to present a single cost preview? Use selected region baseline with note.
- Preemption UX: should preempted jobs be checkpointed automatically (requires infra orchestration)? For MVP, mark as terminate-only; future: coordinated checkpoint + resume.
- RBAC: who can toggle Incident Mode or change policies? Admin vs pool-owner roles.

Proposed acceptance criteria (policy editor MVP):
- Create/update/delete policy UI wiring to backend API (policy saved, applied)
- Slider inputs validated (no negative values, cap <= fleet limits)
- Policy preview shows cost estimate and affected reservations list (sparse data OK)
- Reservation opt-in checkbox is stored and surfaced on reservation details page
- Incident Mode action requires a second confirmation and creates an audit event

Low-fi ASCII sketches (for quick team reference):
[Pool list] | [Policy summary card] | [Preview]
- Pool row: [name] [baseline 8g] [util 72%] [burst 2/4] [⋯]
- Policy card: "Burst policy: Default (active)"
   sliders: |----|----|   max_burst = 4 GPUs

Next steps / owner actions:
- Marisol: convert Primary knobs into real form fields and propose API payload shape (by 2026-02-20)
- Jared: prototype timeline visualization in Figma (by 2026-02-25)
- Priya: validate cost model assumptions with pricing team and provide sample dataset (by 2026-03-01)
- Evan: draft RBAC matrix and incident-mode approval flow (by 2026-03-05)

Notes / references:
- Related: shared_drives/engineering/console-and-tooling/gpu-pool-management-ux-grooming-notes.json (existing pool list ideas)
- Link to runtime PR for preemption hooks: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtimes/pull/1198

Quick UX decisions suggested (call these 'defaults'):
- Default policy: soft-burst enabled, max_burst = min(25% of pool size, 4 GPUs), daily_cost_cap = $100
- Reservation default: burst-opt-in = soft-only
- Incident Mode: manual toggle, max extension +50% for 2 hours limit

Parking lot (non-MVP items):
- Multi-pool burst groups (share burst budgets across pools)
- Predictive autoscale that consumes burst budget proactively for expected spikes
- Fine-grained preemption policies per job type (inference vs training)

Feedback requested:
- Product: is the incident-mode card ok to be in console vs. separate SRE tooling?
- Runtime: what minimal telemetry is required to make preview estimates useful?
- Security/compliance: any concerns with audit trail design for Incident Mode toggles?

End of note.
